There are some coins kept on a table. Ramesh and Suresh decide to play a game. Each one of them, in turn, can pick up any number of coins between 3 and 7(both included). However, if the number of coins available is less than 3, the last person will have to pick them all. The person who makes the last move loses the game. Both of them play intelligently to maximize their chances of winning.

After Suresh’s turn there are 102 coins left on the table. Then in how many cases the coins picked by Suresh ensures his victory irrespective of Ramesh’s moves?

properties.html:
Sportistan, the new country for sportsmen has started a knock-out tournament for all tennis players. The tournament will happen in rounds with initially 128 players participating in the first round. The players are ranked 1 to 128 in descending order of their capabilities with 1 being the best player and 128 being the worst player of the tournament. While scheduling matches “Top meets Bottom” policy is followed. In the first round, Player ranked 1 will play with Player ranked 128 in Match 1, Player Ranked 2 will play with Player ranked 127 in Match 2, Player ranked 3 will play with Player ranked 126 IN Match 3, and so on. The player who loses gets eliminated and the winners move to the 2nd Round. In this round winner of Match 1 and the winner of Match 64 from the first round are paired, the winner of Match 2 and Match 63 from the first round are paired, and so on. This processing continues till only one player emerges as the champion. The round with 8 players and 4 matches is known as the Quarter-Final round and the next two rounds are Semi-Final and Final. If in any match a lower-ranked player defeats a higher-ranked player, that will be known as an “upset”.

If a player ranked 73 reaches Quarter final, which one of the following cannot be his opponent in the Quarter Final match?

properties.html:
There are some coins kept on a table. Ramesh and Suresh decide to play a game. Each one of them, in turn, can pick up any number of coins between 3 and 7(both included). However, if the number of coins available is less than 3, the last person will have to pick them all. The person who makes the last move loses the game. Both of them play intelligently to maximize their chances of winning.

After Suresh’s turn there are 102 coins left on the table. Then in how many cases the coins picked by Suresh ensures his victory irrespective of Ramesh’s moves?

questionFeedback:
Sorry, that's not correct.
Explanation:

The key to solving such questions is that there is a certain sum that the second player can ensure, no matter what the first player picks. Since the minimum coins to be picked is 3 and the maximum is 7, a sum of 10 can always be ensured. For example, if the first player picks 3, the second can pick 7, if the first one picks 4, the second one can pick 6 and so on. Here the number of coins is 102 after Suresh’s turn.             Suresh can always ensure a sum of 10 and he also wants to leave 1/2/3 coins at the end. So if the value after he picks up his coin is of form 10n + 1, 10n + 2 or 10n + 3, Ramesh can win. But leaving the coins in 10n + 1 or 10n + 2 form is not possible as for that, he has to pick 1 and O coins respectively, but the minimum he has to pick is 3. So irrespective of what he picks, he will lose the game.            
So Suresh can pick either 3/4/5/6/7 coins and ensure his win.

questionFeedback:
Sorry, that's not correct.
Explanation:

Whenever n is of the form 10n + 1, 10n + 2, 10n + 3, the person who first picks up the coin, will not be able to win.            
Here k is between 10 and 60, so ‘n’ can range from 1 to 5.            
Hence, the total possible values for which Suresh cannot win are 3 x 5 = 15.

questionFeedback:

In Round 1 player 73 would have met player 56. So he will be the winner of match 56 of the first round. So he will face the winner of match 9 of the first round. So he will be the winner of match 9 of the second round and so on. So basically for a quarter-final 8 players set up, 73 is equivalent to rank 8. So it will face all players who are equivalent to players ranked 1.            
Thus its possible opponents are:

Explanation:

Percentage of students playing any game = 100 – 52 = 48%            
Percentage of students playing both games            
404 + 34 – 48 = 26%
